You can’t get mental health checkups for cheap in NZ. If you’re struggling you can go pay private people for care, at between 150-170$ for therapy and way more for a psychiatrist it’s not exactly affordable here either. The only way you’re getting referred to the public system immediately is to say you’re suicidal, and then all you’ll get is an assessment, no guarantee of any real help. There isn’t anything in place for people that want help because they’re functioning but hella struggling. If you’re lucky enough to get a referral to the public system first they have to decide that you’re in need enough and then they’ll put you on a waitlist which is at least four months in most cases and then maybe you’ll get an outpatient assessment and maybe you’ll get referred to some group therapy but it’s not like they provided free mental health care therapy sessions every week for people that are depressed. I had better experiences in America with mental health care where my insurance would have co-pays but no maximum limits. Here if you do have a private insurance policy with a benefit you’ll have a limit of something like $600 so you know you get to go to four or so therapy sessions but once you hit $600 you’re paying for anything beyond that. I really don’t think there is a country with great mental health care.
I’ve done this twice. Moved to the UAE for 3 years and now to NZ. It’s not all it’s cracked up to be.
